artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $\mathcal{G}(M)$ denote the space of all smooth Riemannian metrics on $M$, equipped with the $C^k$ topology for some $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \infty\}$. For a metric $g \in \mathcal{G}(M)$, let $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$ denote the topological entropy of the geodesic flow of $g$ on the unit tangent bundle $SM$.

Consider the following three density questions about generic dynamical behavior of geodesic flows:

(a) Do the metrics with positive topological entropy, i.e. $\{g \in \mathcal{G}(M) : h_{\mathrm{top}}(g) > 0\}$, form a $C^k$-dense subset of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ for every $k \geq 2$ and every closed manifold $M$ with $\dim M \geq 2$?

(b) Assume $\dim M \geq 3$. Do the metrics $g \in \mathcal{G}(M)$ whose geodesic flow on $SM$ is topologically transitive form a $C^k$-dense subset of $\mathcal{G}(M)$?

(c) Is there a $C^k$-dense subset of metrics $g \in \mathcal{G}(M)$ such that the set of unit tangent vectors to closed geodesics of $g$ is dense in $SM$?

Determine, for each of (a), (b), (c), whether the indicated set of metrics is dense in $\mathcal{G}(M)$ in the $C^k$ topology.
artifact.status_search_result: These are listed as open problems in the Burns–Matveev survey on open problems about geodesics. Partial results are known: positive entropy is $C^2$-dense in all dimensions and $C^\infty$-dense for surfaces; KAM-type obstructions show transitivity fails generically on certain surfaces. The general $C^k$-density questions for $k$ large and higher-dimensional manifolds remain open as of the most recent versions of the survey.
